issues.legal_issue: A lease of immovable property for a term exceeding one year cannot confer enforceable lease rights when it is evidenced by unregistered documents.
material_facts: The firm relied on three written documents as evidence of the lease and its terms.
Under the terms relied on by the firm, the first rent payment covered the period from commencement of the lease through a date fifteen months later.
The documents evidencing the lease were not registered.
issues.conclusion: The lease was for at least fifteen months and required a registered instrument; the firm could not enforce rights under the unregistered lease. Because the firm relied on the documents as evidence of the lease and its terms, it could not avoid registration by contending that they did not constitute the completed lease.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and 2(7) of the Registration Act require registration of an instrument creating a lease for a term exceeding one year. A party relying on written documents as evidence of the lease and its terms cannot avoid that requirement by denying that the documents constitute the completed lease.

rule.if: suit_to_enforce_lease_rights and immovable_property_lease and written_documents_relied_on_as_lease_terms and first_rent_period_exceeds_one_year and lease_documents_unregistered

predicates.suit_to_enforce_lease_rights: A party brought a suit seeking to enforce rights under an asserted lease.
predicates.immovable_property_lease: The asserted lease concerned immovable property.
predicates.written_documents_relied_on_as_lease_ter: The party seeking lease rights relied on written documents as evidence of the lease and its terms.
predicates.first_rent_period_exceeds_one_year: The terms relied on provided for the first rent payment to cover a period exceeding one year from commencement of the lease.
predicates.lease_documents_unregistered: The documents relied on as evidencing the lease were not registered.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to enforce an immovable-property lease on written documents that provide for a first rent period exceeding one year, the absence of registration means lease rights cannot be enforced on that instrument.

issues.legal_issue: An indefinite lease of non-agricultural and non-manufacturing property is not thereby a month-to-month lease when its terms do not indicate monthly tenancy or monthly rent.
material_facts: The firm relied on documents that did not specify a definite overall duration for the lease.
Those documents contained no term indicating that the tenancy was month to month or that rent was payable monthly.
The terms relied on indicated that the first rent payment would be settled at the end of a financial year and covered a period exceeding one year.
There was no pleaded or proved independent basis for finding that a month-to-month lease had arisen.
issues.conclusion: The lease could not be treated as a month-to-month lease under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act merely because its duration was indefinite and the property was not used for agricultural or manufacturing purposes.
issues.legal_principle: Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 does not make an indefinite lease a month-to-month tenancy on those facts alone; the terms or other evidence must support that characterization. Ram Kumar Das v. Jagadish Chandra Deb Dhabal Deb was distinguished because there, other evidence supported a monthly tenancy and monthly rent.

rule.if: lease_dispute and lease_duration_indefinite and no_monthly_tenancy_term_or_monthly_rent and no_independent_month_to_month_evidence

predicates.lease_dispute: The dispute concerns the duration and character of an asserted lease.
predicates.lease_duration_indefinite: The lease terms do not specify a definite overall duration.
predicates.no_monthly_tenancy_term_or_monthly_rent: The terms do not state that the tenancy is month to month or that rent is payable monthly.
predicates.no_independent_month_to_month_evidence: No other pleaded or proved evidence establishes a month-to-month tenancy.

issues.definition: An indefinite lease is not treated as month to month when its terms and the other evidence do not establish monthly tenancy or monthly rent.

issues.legal_issue: The protection against enforcement of rights by a lessor under part performance is a defence and does not give a lessee an affirmative right to enforce an unregistered lease.
material_facts: The firm had taken possession of two portions of the property but had not taken possession of the third portion.
The firm brought a suit seeking possession and other reliefs by enforcing rights under the unregistered lease.
The claim in the suit was affirmative enforcement of lease rights, not merely a defence against the lessor's attempt to enforce rights.
issues.conclusion: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act did not allow the firm to claim possession or other affirmative relief under the unregistered lease.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 bars a transferor from enforcing rights against a transferee who has taken possession in part performance; it is available as a defence and does not confer an affirmative cause of action to enforce an unregistered lease. The Court relied on Probodh Kumar Das v. Dantmara Tea Company Ltd. and distinguished Ram Chander v. Maharaj Kunwar, without expressing an opinion on the correctness of that decision; it also explained that the latter case involved a plaintiff acting in substance as a defendant to protect possession.

predicates.lessee_sues_to_affirmatively_enforce_unr: A lessee brought a suit seeking affirmative relief based on an unregistered lease.
predicates.lessee_took_possession_of_some_property: The lessee had taken possession of some, but not necessarily all, of the property covered by the asserted lease.

issues.definition: When a lessee sues affirmatively to enforce an unregistered lease after taking possession of some of the property, part-performance protection does not provide the requested affirmative lease rights.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance of an unregistered lease contract under the statutory provision for part performance is unavailable when specific performance is not claimed, the entire contract is not in writing, or the lessee has not taken possession of the entire property.
material_facts: The firm sought possession, damages and injunctions, but did not claim specific performance in its plaint.
The firm's own case was that the entire contract was not contained in the three written documents and was completed later through further corporate authorization and the giving of possession.
The contract concerned three portions of property, but the firm took possession of only two and never obtained possession of the third.
The firm argued in the alternative that the documents constituted a written agreement to lease and could be specifically enforced.
issues.conclusion: Specific performance could not be granted: it was not claimed in the plaint, the firm's own case was that the entire contract was not in writing, and possession had not been taken of the entire property covered by the contract.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27A of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 applies to an unregistered lease contract only where the whole contract is in writing and the lessee has taken possession of the property, or continues in possession in part performance. Unlike section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, section 27A does not extend to possession of only part of the property; the Court relied on the contrast between the provisions' wording.

rule.if: suit_seeks_enforcement_of_lease_contract and unregistered_lease_contract and (not specific_performance_prayed_for or not whole_contract_in_writing or not entire_property_possession_taken)

predicates.suit_seeks_enforcement_of_lease_contract: A party brought a suit seeking relief based on an asserted lease contract.
predicates.unregistered_lease_contract: The lease contract was not registered.
predicates.specific_performance_prayed_for: The party expressly requested specific performance in the pleadings.
predicates.whole_contract_in_writing: The entire lease contract was set out in writing.
predicates.entire_property_possession_taken: The lessee took possession of all the property covered by the lease contract, or continued in possession of all of it in part performance.

issues.definition: Specific performance of an unregistered lease contract is unavailable when it is not requested, the entire contract is not written, or the lessee has not taken possession of all the property covered by the contract.
